name: Idempotency keys DLQ poison queues
short_definition: At-least-once delivery is the default for queues and flaky networks: make handlers idempotent with durable idempotency keys, classify errors for bounded retries with backoff, and route exhausted/poison messages to a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for inspection — never infinite retry storms.
scope_in: Idempotency-Key on HTTP APIs; job/webhook dedupe tables; retry budgets and exponential backoff + jitter; transient vs permanent errors; DLQ/poison queue design; outbox pattern for reliable publish; Stripe/webhook style event ids; Temporal activity idempotency notes; observability of retries/DLQ depth.
scope_out: Choosing Taskiq vs Celery vs Temporal (py-background-jobs); full payment domain rules (billing modules); pure in-request anyio retries without durability; load balancer retries configuration deep-dive.
defaults: Assume at-least-once: every side-effecting consumer (HTTP handler with money/state, queue worker, webhook) is idempotent. Store idempotency keys (client key or event id) in Postgres with unique constraint + request hash + response snapshot (or processing status). Retries: only transient errors (network, 503, deadlock, lock timeout); max attempts (e.g. 5) with exponential backoff + full jitter; permanent errors (validation, 4xx business) fail fast to DLQ or error status without requeue loops. DLQ: preserve payload, error, attempt count, first/last failure timestamps, correlation id; alert on depth. Outbox: write domain row + outbox event in one transaction; publisher worker drains outbox. Webhooks: verify signature first, then dedupe by provider event id. Pass the same idempotency key to external providers (Stripe etc.) across retries.
decision_gates: USE idempotency keys when: POST that creates resources, payments, enqueue-once, webhook receivers, any client-retried mutating API. USE automatic retries when: error is transient and operation is idempotent or safely reentrant. USE DLQ when: attempts exhausted or message poison (deserialize fail, invariant break). USE Temporal when: multi-step with built-in retry policies per activity — still design activities idempotent. DO NOT retry non-idempotent charges without key. DO NOT infinite retry. DO NOT ack-before-process if loss is unacceptable without another durability layer.
do_dont: DO: unique(event_id) / unique(idempotency_key, user_scope); compare payload hash on replay; return stored response on duplicate key; log attempt n/max; metric DLQ depth; jitter backoff. DON'T: retry on all Exception; sleep unbounded in hot consumers without isolation; drop poison messages silently; generate new idempotency key per retry to external APIs; process webhook before signature verify; use only in-memory dedupe for multi-instance workers.
failure_modes: 1) Duplicate side effects from retries without keys. 2) Idempotency key reused with different body → silent wrong response if not hashed. 3) Infinite retry hammering dependency. 4) Retrying permanent 400s. 5) Lost poison messages with no DLQ. 6) Race: two workers pass dedupe without unique constraint. 7) Outbox not same transaction as state change. 8) Generating new provider idempotency key on each attempt. 9) DLQ without alerts (silent backlog). 10) Returning 200 on webhook before durable persist.
anti_patterns: except Exception: retry; Redis SET without TTL policy for forever keys on high cardinality without plan; dedupe only in process memory; DLQ as black hole with no runbook; client retries + server retries without budgets (thundering herd); non-idempotent 'increment balance' without ledger key; catch-all retry on CancelledError.
tools: Postgres unique constraints for idempotency/outbox; Redis for short-TTL locks optional; queue DLX (RabbitMQ), Redis failed lists / custom DLQ streams, SQS redrive; Taskiq/Celery retry middleware; Temporal RetryPolicy; Stripe Idempotency-Key header; structlog + metrics (retry_count, dlq_depth). Testing: pytest concurrency for unique races.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13: Patterns stable and tool-agnostic. Celery/Taskiq/arq each expose retry hooks differently — encode policy in app middleware. HTTP Idempotency-Key is industry practice (Stripe-style). Temporal docs: generate provider idempotency keys inside durable steps so retries reuse keys. Review broker-specific DLQ config when pinning broker version.

# Alert: dlq_depth > 0 for 5m → page
deprecation_watch: Ack-before-work defaults without compensating idempotency; infinite Celery autoretry for all exceptions; 'exactly once' claims from brokers without handler design; Memory-only idempotency caches as sole guard; swallowing DLQ messages in cron without metrics.
ts_boundary: Next/BFF should send Idempotency-Key on mutating POSTs to Python; regenerate same key on client retry (uuid per user intent, not per HTTP attempt). Webhooks preferably hit one backend (TS or Python) — single consumer with dedupe. Align error codes so clients know safe retry (409/425 vs 500).
rust_boundary: Same idempotency table or Redis key space if multi-language consumers — coordinate key namespaces. Prefer one consumer language per event type to avoid dual processing. Durable ledgers for money may live in Rust with explicit keys.
supabase_boundary: Store idempotency and webhook_events tables with RLS denying client writes (service only) or pure service_role access. Unique constraints are the source of truth for dedupe. Realtime not for dedupe. Migrations for these tables go through owned migration path.
boundary_contracts: Idempotency-Key header contract on OpenAPI for mutating routes; webhook event_id documented; outbox schema; env retry budgets; MCP tools that mutate must accept idempotency or be read-only. DLQ message schema versioned.
decision_matrix_row: Problem: client double-submit payment → Idempotency-Key + ledger. Problem: queue redelivery → handler idempotent + unique event id. Problem: flaky upstream → bounded retry + backoff. Problem: bad payload forever → DLQ + alert. Problem: multi-step money move → Temporal/saga + per-activity idempotency.
threats: Replay attacks on webhooks without signature+dedupe; idempotency key flooding (storage DoS); cache poisoning if key not scoped to user; forcing retries to amplify expensive side effects; log injection via error bodies in DLQ.
mitigations: Signature verification before dedupe insert; scope keys to principal; TTL or retention job on idempotency rows; rate limit POST; authorize enqueue; redact PII in DLQ tools; alert and bound DLQ size; authz on replay tools.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST: idempotent workers; unique constraints; classify transient vs permanent; max attempts + jitter; DLQ with context; webhook signature then dedupe; reuse external idempotency keys across retries. MUST NOT: retry all exceptions infinitely; ack then process without durability plan for critical work; silent drop; new random key per external retry; process webhook without verify.
tests_required: Concurrent double POST same Idempotency-Key → one side effect; key reuse different body → 409; webhook duplicate event_id → no double apply; retry budget stops at max; permanent error no retry; outbox publish atomicity test; DLQ written after exhaustion.
ci_gates: pytest concurrency/idempotency tests; migration for unique keys present; ban bare except Exception retry loops via lint/grep; optional chaos test in staging.
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: Idempotency-Key, unique event_id, classify/retry budget, dlq.publish, outbox table, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, backoff jitter. NEGATIVE: while True retry, except Exception: continue retry, no dedupe on webhooks, BackgroundTasks for payment, generate uuid() inside retry loop for Stripe key, empty except on poison.
skill_module_bullets:
- At-least-once: design idempotent handlers always.
- Idempotency-Key + request hash + durable store for mutating APIs.
- Webhooks: verify signature → dedupe event id → apply.
- Retry only transient errors; max attempts; exponential backoff + jitter.
- DLQ poison messages with payload + error + alert on depth.
- Outbox for DB+publish atomicity.
- Reuse provider idempotency keys across attempts — never regenerate per retry.
action_items: 1) Standard idempotency SQL + middleware snippet in skill. 2) Scan webhook handlers for missing dedupe. 3) Document retry classification table. 4) Cross-link py-background-jobs and billing-stripe. 5) DLQ alert template in deploy-ops.

conflicts_noted: Brokers advertise different delivery guarantees; application idempotency remains mandatory. Some teams prefer Redis-only idempotency keys — fine with TTL and multi-instance atomicity (SET NX) but Postgres unique is stronger for money. Celery ack-early vs late: configure explicitly; do not rely on defaults. Temporal reduces custom retry code but does not remove activity idempotency needs.
